file_roles.evidence: The reported failure is an SSL stream condition, 'Code:9001, Message:"Write results unavailable from localhost:27026 :: caused by :: asio.ssl stream truncated"', and the single non-test gold file is the server's asio SSL I/O detail header, the layer that drives the SSL read/write loop and decides when a truncated stream is an error. No other non-test file changed, so the mishandling of that condition is here.

rationale: The reporter sees error 9001 with 'asio.ssl stream truncated' from the Go driver during TestCollection_InsertMany_Batches, 'only ... on macOS', so the condition arises on a large multi-batch write over TLS. The one non-test gold file is src/mongo/util/net/ssl/detail/io.hpp, the asio SSL I/O layer that raises and acts on stream_truncated, so the condition surfaces and is mishandled at the same place. Two of the three changed files were tests and are already filtered out of the gold set.
notes: NO-DIFF PACKET: every gold file in this packet shows '(no diff retrieved)' and the fix commit message is '(empty)', so the issue report is the only evidence the packet carries. Decision recorded here per CONVENTIONS.md ('If a case is not covered here, follow RUBRIC.md and say in notes what was decided and why'): a role is assigned only where the report itself names the faulty code, the wrong behaviour, or the adopted fix, and every other gold file is 'unclear', per schema.json ('A label without citable evidence is not auditable and must be unclear'). Instance confidence is capped at medium because no diff was shown. The pasted output belongs to another project and to the reporter's own code: it is a Go driver struct dump, 'mongo.BulkWriteError{WriteErrors:mongo.WriteErrors{...}}', from the Go driver's own unit test, not from the mongodb server. log_location is not determinable: no server log line is shown and the quoted text is a client-side error value. The gold file does not appear in the report at all; it is matched to the failure only through the string 'asio.ssl stream truncated' naming the asio SSL layer, and the packet did not show the source tree. Note also that this gold file is vendored third-party asio code carried inside the mongo tree, which is worth knowing when a localizer is scored on it. A second rater could reasonably call this 'symptom-handling', since the change may only alter how a truncated stream is reported; it is causal here because no other non-test file was changed and so nothing else was treated as broken.
